## Monongahela National Forest

Biophysical Settings describe the vegetation a place would have supported before Euro-American settlement, given the land and its historical disturbance regime. This summary covers Monongahela National Forest. The [table](inputs/bps_monongahela.csv) is one row per setting.

```{r}
#| label: bps-chart
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-cap: "Ten largest Biophysical Settings on Monongahela National Forest."
#| fig-alt: "Horizontal bar chart of the ten most extensive Biophysical Settings. Spruce-fir forest is the longest bar, followed by dry-mesic oak forest."

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

bps <- read.csv("inputs/bps_monongahela.csv")

# Map-zone variants can share a name. Sum acres, then keep the top 10.
top10 <- bps |>
  group_by(BPS_NAME, GROUPVEG) |>
  summarize(ACRES = sum(ACRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  slice_max(order_by = ACRES, n = 10)

top_row <- top10 |> slice_max(order_by = ACRES, n = 1)

group_colors <- c(
  "Conifer" = "#1B6B3A",
  "Hardwood" = "#C47B2B",
  "Hardwood-Conifer" = "#6B4C2A",
  "Riparian" = "#2E86AB",
  "Open Water" = "#7FB3D5",
  "Savanna" = "#D4A017",
  "Barren-Rock/Sand/Clay" = "#7F8C8D"
)

ggplot(top10, aes(x = reorder(BPS_NAME, ACRES), y = ACRES, fill = GROUPVEG)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_comma(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.06))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = group_colors) +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 historical ecosystems",
    subtitle = "Monongahela National Forest",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Acres",
    fill = "Vegetation group"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

`r top_row$BPS_NAME` covers the most ground in this summary, about `r scales::comma(round(top_row$ACRES))` acres. Oak forests and Appalachian (hemlock)–northern hardwood forest follow. Riparian systems and rocky oak-pine woodland are on the forest too, on much less area.

## Wooden Man Weather

[Wooden Man Weather](https://rswaty.github.io/woodenmanweather/) is a dashboard for Marquette and the central Upper Peninsula. It is built to be checked: the forecast beside the recent year, and how that year compares with normal. Same publishing tool as this site, different pace.
